The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
The U.S. Army says it will carry out the detonation of nearly five tons of unstable
lead azide today at an Army ammunition plant in southeast Iowa. It's a compound used in explosives.
Tom Barton with Iowa Public Radio reports some local residents are being advised to leave the
area temporarily. The Army says the material had been stored for decades at the Middletown plant
and formed crystals inside the drums, sensitive to shock, friction and temperature. The Army says
it considered chemical treatment but concluded the drums were too dangerous to open or move.
Acting Army Secretary Adam Tell says federal agencies agree a plant blast is the safest
option. We don't want to give the public the feeling that there's absolutely no risk.
The public needs to know what risk we understand and take precaution to protect themselves against
any risk they perceive. We're going to provide that information to them so they can make that
decision. The Army is urging residents in Middletown and in a zone extending about five miles southwest
of the plant to leave temporarily. For NPR News, I'm Tom Barton in Des Moines. The White House is
proposing a new set of tariffs on goods from more than a dozen countries including China, Japan,
India and also the EU citing unfair trade practices. This is President Trump doubles
down on the levies despite several of them previously being struck down by the Supreme Court.
Republicans have lost a U.S. House seat in Tennessee according to an Associated Press
race call. From member station WPLN, Mariana Bakayau has more. Victoria Broderick's ascension
to Congress upends the Tennessee GOP's plan of sending an all-Republican delegation to Washington.
She beat the Republican incumbent after state lawmakers redrew the congressional maps to
eliminate Memphis's Democratic seat. Broderick narrowly won with less than $100,000 raised.
She says she's won by being an average person focused on the cost of living.
Rich people aren't thinking about milk and eggs. She now makes history as the first woman to
represent the fourth congressional district and the first openly queer person ever elected
to Congress from Tennessee. For NPR News, I'm Mariana Bakayau in Nashville. King Tides flooded
low-lying areas along the California coast yesterday. Ezra David Romero from member
station KQED has more. At over eight feet, King Tides pushed San Francisco to break a monthly
record for the highest tide ever in November. That's partly because El Nino raised local
sea levels a foot or more. Tides are forecast to be even taller and could come close to its
all-time record setback in 1983. Here's San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie. I want everybody
to enjoy Thanksgiving, but we expect more rain in the coming months and these King Tides are
only going to get higher. Even taller Tides are expected around Christmas. For NPR News,
I'm Ezra David Romero in San Francisco. You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
In the latest in a series of computer problems in government organizations and high-profile
private companies, the CIA has been hacked. According to a person with knowledge of the
breach who was not authorized to speak publicly, it happened in an unclassified part of the CIA's
computer system and no classified parts of the network were affected. Earlier, several big
companies including Microsoft, Apple, and major banks were hit with system-wide computer failures
this month along with a national security agency. But those outages were attributed to internal
patch or software upgrade flaws. It's not clear who's behind the CIA hack. The vaccine non-profit
Gavi has committed to buying up to one and a half million doses of a new Ebola vaccine. As
Impiers Jonathan Lambert reports, the bulk purchased by the funder will help more people
get the vaccine if it is shown to be safe and effective. There are currently no licensed
vaccines for the kind of Ebola that's spreading in the Democratic Republic of Congo called
Bundabujo. A clinical trial in DRC is currently testing an Ebola vaccine targeting a different
species and two new Bundabujo-specific vaccines are set to enter trials in the coming days.
Even if these vaccine candidates end up working, they're not going to do much good unless there's
a large supply. Gavi announced a deal with the Serum Institute of India, the vaccine maker,
to secure over a million doses of the vaccine candidate developed by the University of Oxford.
Now, the Serum Institute can start making lots of doses so they can be sent to DRC
if the vaccine gets approved. Jonathan Lambert, NPR News. And I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News in
Washington. This message comes from Midi Health. Most women never get real answers about their
